 : Judgment :

The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No.
LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/13(A)/2011-12 dated 16.03.2021 in respect of Sy. No.83/1 measuring 101 Sq.
meters of Chikkajala village and Jalahalli Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka, Bengaluru Urban District.

.2. The definite case of the petitioner is that the property bearing Sy. No.83/1 measuring 101 Sq.
meters situated at Chikkajala village and Jala Hobli has been A.P. No.98/2022 acquired under Gazette notification No. S.O. No.1622(E) dated 02.07.2010.
Prior to that Preliminary Notification issued under S.O. No.3159(E) dated 09.12.2009.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.4,99,160/- as compensation for 101 Sq. meters of the land belongs to the petitioner.
The petitioner received the same under protest and filed an application on 21.09.2011 for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.8,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.

.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are contrary to law, hence the claim of the claimant cannot be sustainable in law.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for enhanced compensation and the claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained in law.

Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the compensation awarded by the respondent No. 1 is in A.P. No.98/2022 accordance with the provisions of the said Act and does not call for interference in the interest of justice.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.

.4. Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR- 104/13(A)/103/2011-12, 65/2012-13 dated 16.03.2021.
.5.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 is wholly erroneous, contrary to law, materials on record and in violation of principles of natural justice and the same is liable to be set aside.

sentences.text: respondent No.3 committed a legal misconduct in not following the documents filed by the petitioner for deciding the market value.
The Arbitrator A.P. No.98/2022 failed to appreciate the fact that the respondent No. 3 has not produced any documents to justify the award passed by him.
The award dated 13.12.2020 passed by the respondent No. 2 is not in accordance with the guidance value under Section 3G(7) of NH Act.
The award amount is not at all matching with the market value for prime land of the petitioner.

The land acquired is more than value than the award amount, even the enhanced just and meager compensation without taken into consideration material evidence placed before the Court, which is against probabilities of the case.
The respondent No. 3 grossly erred in considering the fact that the acquired land situated very near to Bengaluru International Airport and situated amidst the lands commercially developed.

The LAO and Arbitrator has not recorded any evidence and not considered for payment of solatium on the award amount and additional market value along with interest from the date of taking possession till the A.P. No.98/2022 date of payment.
Accordingly, prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.

.6. The respondent No.1 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/
respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
A.P. No.98/2022 .7.
The petitioner along with the petition filed I.A. No. 1 under Section 34(3) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, for condonation of delay if any filing the petition.

.8. The above application is supported with the affidavit of petitioner, wherein, it is stated that the order has not been communicated to him and when he approached the concerned authority on 18.04.2022, he came to know about the order and he immediately applied for copy of the order and he got the same on 26.05.2022.

Thereafter, filed this petition and accordingly prayed for condonation of delay if any in filing the petition.
.9.
The respondent No.1 has not filed any objections to the IA.
.10. The respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their Advocate.
The respondent No.3 appeared through ADGP, but not resisted the petition.

The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.12,973/- per Sq. meters from Rs.4,942/- per Sq. meters and awarded additional compensation of Rs. 8031/- per Sq. meters as per table shown in the award.

The said claim of the petitioner is also found in the award.

sentences.text:
Admittedly in the case on hand, the LAO awarded the compensation of Rs.4,942/- per Sq. Meter and it is A.P.
No.98/2022 enhanced to the tune of Rs.12,973/- per Sq. Meter by enhancing only Rs.8,031/- per Sq. Meter as per table in the award.
Even it is considered, the Arbitrator considered the claim of petitioner in his order and enhanced almost 3 times.
The compensation awarded by the LAO is at Rs. 4,942/- per Sq. meter that has been enhanced to Rs. 12,873/- per Sq. meter.
The petitioner has not placed any material before the Court to show that the market value can be enhanced more than Rs. 8,031/- per Sq. meter.
Even there is no material on record to show that the market value has been enhanced for more than Rs. 12,973/- per Sq. meter.

Under such circumstance, the Court cannot find any fault in findings of the Arbitrator, as such, certainly there is no material whatsoever on record to show to intervene with the order of Arbitrator and the Arbitrator considered all material fact and evidence placed before him while passing the order.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the negative.
.21. Point No.3:
In view of my above findings, I proceed to pass the following.
A.P. No.98/2022 ORDER IA filed by the petitioner to condone the delay in filing the petition is allowed.
Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.

Consequently, the impugned award passed by the respondent No.3 in case No.LAQ / ARB / NH-7 /
CR / 13(A) / 2011- 12 dated 16.03.2021 in respect of Sy.
No.83/1 measuring 101 Sq. meters of Chikkajala village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Addl. Taluka,
Bengaluru Urban District is confirmed.
Parties to bear their own cost.
Send back the records.
